    18  
    19  This file defines typeclasses to reason about monotonicity of the operations
    20  * `b ↦ a • b`, "left scalar multiplication"
    21  * `a ↦ a • b`, "right scalar multiplication"
    22  
    23  We use eight typeclasses to encode the various properties we care about for those two operations.
    24  These typeclasses are meant to be mostly internal to this file, to set up each lemma in the
    25  appropriate generality.
    26  
    27  Less granular typeclasses like `IsOrderedAddMonoid` and `IsOrderedModule` should be enough for most
    28  purposes, and the system is set up so that they imply the correct granular typeclasses here.
    29  If those are enough for you, you may stop reading here! Else, beware that what
    30  follows is a bit technical.
    31  
    32  
    33  In all that follows, `α` and `β` are orders which have a `0` and such that `α` acts on `β` by scalar
    34  multiplication. Note however that we do not use lawfulness of this action in most of the file. Hence
    35  `•` should be considered here as a mostly arbitrary function `α → β → β`.
    36  
    37  We use the following four typeclasses to reason about left scalar multiplication (`b ↦ a • b`):
    38  * `PosSMulMono`: If `a ≥ 0`, then `b₁ ≤ b₂` implies `a • b₁ ≤ a • b₂`.
    39  * `PosSMulStrictMono`: If `a > 0`, then `b₁ < b₂` implies `a • b₁ < a • b₂`.
    40  * `PosSMulReflectLT`: If `a ≥ 0`, then `a • b₁ < a • b₂` implies `b₁ < b₂`.
    41  * `PosSMulReflectLE`: If `a > 0`, then `a • b₁ ≤ a • b₂` implies `b₁ ≤ b₂`.
    42  
    43  We use the following four typeclasses to reason about right scalar multiplication (`a ↦ a • b`):
    44  * `SMulPosMono`: If `b ≥ 0`, then `a₁ ≤ a₂` implies `a₁ • b ≤ a₂ • b`.
    45  * `SMulPosStrictMono`: If `b > 0`, then `a₁ < a₂` implies `a₁ • b < a₂ • b`.
    46  * `SMulPosReflectLT`: If `b ≥ 0`, then `a₁ • b < a₂ • b` implies `a₁ < a₂`.
    47  * `SMulPosReflectLE`: If `b > 0`, then `a₁ • b ≤ a₂ • b` implies `a₁ ≤ a₂`.
    48  
    49  Furthermore, in a *module*, i.e. a group acted on by a ring, `PosSMulMono` and `SMulPosMono` are
    50  equivalent (they are both the same as `∀ r ≥ 0, ∀ m ≥ 0, 0 ≤ r • m`),
